record_reviews.summary: Airy's 53-paragraph treatise proposes that alternate distichous leaf order (1/2) is ancestral to spiral orders and collateral distichous order to whorls. He argues bud condensation responds to frost/heat and other pressures, compares elm, beech, fir, sunflower, roots and cactus, and uses oak-gall models with longitudinal contraction to derive 1/3, 2/5, 3/8 and higher orders. He closes with speculative leaf/root homologies and asks Darwin's opinion. Five diagrams are preserved; one inspected shows paired leaves along a stem, while the prose and annotations identify additional model/leaf-order drawings.
record_reviews.date_assessment: Before 15 July 1872; XML runs from the generic 1809 lower artifact to 14 July 1872. The long essay is an incoming Airy proposal, not an 1851–55 source.
record_reviews.attribution_assessment: Surviving prose is attributed to Airy, Hubert addressing Darwin, C. R.; direction is to_darwin. Scholarly notes, annotations, footnotes and bibliography were read separately; quoted Donders material in 7452 remains an embedded voice.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin asks Bowman to read a copied slip from Donders about tear secretion and orbicular spasm, asks about analogous cases, and reasons through tears during yawning and tickling. The French enclosure is preserved as a separate scholarly section and is translated in a later editorial footnote; it is not Darwin's voice. The source includes an unavailable original Donders letter behind that extract.

record_reviews.summary: Bowman's ten-paragraph medical response discusses lacrimation from dust, corneal irritation, photophobia, accommodation strain and internal eye disease, distinguishing conjunctival/corneal causes from retinal and optic-nerve disease. He offers to observe matters from Darwin's perspective and states belief in development. The body has many supplied lacunae and is an incomplete 12-page ALS; the missing Darwin inquiry is not preserved.
